name: The Meridian Hunger Games — Annual Synth Cuisine Competition
creator: Axiom Network One, produced by Coldframe Corporate Media Solutions
description: Officially titled the Meridian Synthesis Open but universally called the Hunger Games since its second season, this annual competitive cooking broadcast airs on Axiom Network One as a neural-feed event reaching an estimated 4.2 million concurrent viewers at peak. Thirty-two competitors drawn from all tiers — with tokenistic the Gray Zone representation that has been widely criticized — compete over six weeks to create dishes that are judged on flavor, nutrition efficiency, cost-per-serving, and 'synthesis innovation,' the last category defined entirely by a rotating corporate judging panel. The show's central tension is that Tier 1 and Tier 2 competitors must work with synth-protein baseline ingredients while Tier 4-5 competitors can purchase real-ingredient upgrades using a budget allocation system that mirrors real economic inequality almost perfectly.
cultural_impact: The show is one of Axiom's highest-rated properties and functions as a significant vehicle for normalizing synth-protein cuisine as aspirational rather than merely adequate — a framing that critics argue serves corponation food-production interests directly. It is also genuinely watched and debated across all tiers, making it a rare shared cultural text in a city where most media consumption is tier-segregated.
controversy: Season 9 (2210) produced the show's defining controversy when the Gray Zone competitor Yusra Mensah-Kowalczyk won the technical round with a fermented synth-offal dish that judges initially praised before the final episode revealed the judging panel had been overruled by an Axiom executive who awarded the season prize to a Tier 4 competitor. Mensah-Kowalczyk's post-show interview, in which she said simply 'I cooked better food,' was viewed 11 million times on pirate neural feeds.
story_hooks: A the Gray Zone competitor in the current season is cooking dishes that contain trace compounds not present in any registered synth-protein product — and someone in the production team is trying to quietly identify the source before the feed goes live.

Yusra Mensah-Kowalczyk, four years after her Season 9 controversy, has been invited back as a judge — and someone wants her to either rehabilitate the show's reputation or burn it down, and will pay accordingly.

An investigative journalist discovers that the 'Tier 1 competitor' in the current season is not actually from the Gray Zone — their backstory, poverty credentials, and the Gray Zone accent are all carefully constructed by a Coldframe casting producer chasing demographics.
